templates.internal_notes_hr: Confirm COMPASS / Fair Consideration where applicable; check DP needs early.
watchouts: EP processing can take several weeks; start once salary and role classification are firm.
Dependant passes add parallel documentation (marriage/birth certificates, translations).
IPA validity window is tight — align travel and entry dates with HR.

templates.route_title: United Kingdom — Skilled Worker visa (sponsored route)
templates.employee_summary: Your employer holds a sponsor licence and will assign you a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS). You then apply for a Skilled Worker visa before travelling to the UK. ReloPass tracks each step so nothing slips.
templates.hr_summary: Confirm sponsor licence is active, assign an undefined or defined CoS as appropriate, and support the employee's visa application. Right-to-work check on Day 1 is mandatory.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Check CoS assignment lead time (defined CoS needs Home Office approval, ~5 business days). Ensure salary meets minimum threshold for role SOC code. BRP collection from Post Office within 10 days of arrival.
watchouts: CoS must be assigned before the employee submits their visa application — allow at least 1 week buffer.
Salary must meet both the general threshold and the specific SOC code going rate; verify before issuing CoS.
BRP card is sent to a UK address — employee must collect within 10 days of arrival.
Right-to-work check must be completed on or before Day 1; share code expires in 90 days.

checklist.title: Formal offer letter confirming role, salary & SOC code
checklist.notes_employee: Required for CoS assignment and visa application.
checklist.notes_hr: Salary must satisfy both general threshold and going rate for the SOC code.

checklist.notes_employee: You will need the CoS reference number to apply for your visa.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)

checklist.title: English language evidence

checklist.notes_hr: Exempt if national of majority English-speaking country.

checklist.notes_employee: £1,270 in bank for 28 consecutive days unless employer certifies maintenance.
checklist.notes_hr: Certify maintenance on CoS to remove this requirement for the employee.

checklist.title: Online visa application submitted & biometrics booked
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at least 3 months before start date. Biometrics at UKVCAS service point.
checklist.notes_hr: Provide IHS surcharge payment confirmation number if employer covers it.

checklist.title: Skilled Worker visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check vignette dates — first entry must be on or before the valid from date.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy for sponsor compliance file.

checklist.notes_employee: Use the UKVI online share code to allow HR to verify.
checklist.notes_hr: Statutory excuse requires online check for visa nationals — record date and outcome.

milestones.body_hr: Confirm BRP collected; file copy; schedule 6-month compliance check.

templates.route_title: Germany — EU Blue Card / Skilled Worker Visa
templates.employee_summary: Your employer will sponsor either an EU Blue Card (for high earners) or a Skilled Worker Visa under Germany's Fachkräftezuwanderungsgesetz. You apply at the German consulate before travelling, then complete Anmeldung and the residence permit after arrival.
templates.hr_summary: Confirm visa route based on salary and qualification recognition status. Support the employee's consulate application and ensure Anmeldung and Ausländerbehörde steps are completed promptly after arrival.
templates.internal_notes_hr: EU Blue Card requires salary ≥ €45,300 (2024 threshold) or €56,400 for shortage occupations. Qualification recognition may take 4–12 weeks — start early. Anmeldung must be done within 14 days of arrival.
watchouts: Qualification recognition (Anerkennung) can be the critical-path item — initiate before the consulate appointment.
Anmeldung must be completed within 14 days of arrival; the confirmation letter (Anmeldebestätigung) is needed for the Aufenthaltstitel and bank accounts.
Statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) must be in place before the Ausländerbehörde appointment.
EU Blue Card holders can bring family without a separate income threshold — a useful selling point.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract confirming salary and role
checklist.notes_employee: Required for visa application and qualification recognition.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm salary meets Blue Card or Skilled Worker threshold.

checklist.notes_employee: Submit via anabin database or relevant chamber. Allow 4–12 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for regulated professions and Blue Card applications.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay.

checklist.notes_hr: Track application reference number.

checklist.notes_employee: Check visa validity dates and permitted activities.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy for HR file.

checklist.notes_employee: Must be in place before the Ausländerbehörde appointment.
checklist.notes_hr: Check employer's health insurance contribution obligations.

checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Ausländerbehörde. Bring: passport, Anmeldebestätigung, contract, health insurance proof.
checklist.notes_hr: Process can take 4–8 weeks; employee may work in the meantime if visa permits.

checklist.title: Housing & schooling shortlist (if family)
checklist.notes_employee: Family members need separate Aufenthaltstitel — apply at the same time.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm relocation budget covers family costs.

templates.route_title: Norway — Skilled Worker Permit / EEA Registration
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals need a Skilled Worker Permit (faglært arbeidstillatelse) applied through UDI before or shortly after arrival. EU/EEA nationals register a certificate of residence (registreringsbevis) at Statsforvalteren. Both groups need a tax card (Skattekort) and Folkeregisteret address registration before payroll can run.
templates.hr_summary: Confirm nationality to choose the correct route (UDI permit vs EU/EEA registration). Initiate UDI application as soon as the job offer is signed — processing times vary from 1–12 weeks. Ensure Skattekort and Folkeregisteret steps are completed before first pay date.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Skilled Worker Permit requires a concrete job offer with Norwegian standard salary. EU/EEA registration is simpler but still requires proof of employment. D-number is issued first; fødselsnummer comes after 6 months of registered residence.
watchouts: UDI processing for Skilled Worker Permits can take 1–12 weeks — apply immediately after job offer is signed.
Skattekort must be obtained before first payroll run; delays cause higher withholding tax (50%).
Folkeregisteret address registration must be done within 8 days of establishing residence.
D-number is issued for short stays; fødselsnummer (permanent ID) is issued after 6 months — bank accounts often require the latter.

checklist.notes_employee: Obtain at skatteetaten.no before first payroll — without it, 50% tax is withheld.
checklist.notes_hr: Payroll cannot run correctly without Skattekort on file.

checklist.notes_employee: Register within 8 days of establishing Norwegian residence. Bring housing contract.

checklist.notes_employee: Most banks require D-number or fødselsnummer; some accept passport for initial account.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for salary payment to Norwegian account.

checklist.title: Housing & schooling shortlist (if family)
checklist.notes_employee: Family members require separate immigration applications — apply in parallel.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm relocation budget covers family costs.

templates.route_title: Brazil — VITEM V Work Visa / CRNM
templates.employee_summary: Your employer must first obtain work authorisation from Brazil's Ministry of Labour (SINFRE/MTE), which unlocks your VITEM V (temporary worker) visa at the consulate. After arrival, you must register with the Federal Police within 90 days to obtain your CRNM (national migration registration card) and then obtain a CPF (tax ID) with Receita Federal.
templates.hr_summary: Initiate the MTE employer authorisation as the critical path item — this can take 4–8 weeks before the employee can even apply at the consulate. Ensure CRNM and CPF steps are completed within 90 days of arrival to maintain legal status.
templates.internal_notes_hr: VITEM V is the standard route for employed workers. The CRNM replaces the old RNE card. CPF is required for bank accounts, payroll, and any Brazilian contracts. CTPS (Carteira de Trabalho) digital registration with the employer is also required. Private health insurance is strongly recommended as public SUS access for foreigners is limited.
watchouts: Ministry of Labour (MTE/SINFRE) authorisation is the critical path — allow 4–8 weeks before consulate application.
CRNM Federal Police registration must be completed within 90 days of first entry or legal status lapses.
CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas) is required for payroll, bank accounts, and almost all official transactions.
CTPS (digital employment card) must be registered with the employer at hiring.
Private health insurance is strongly recommended; public SUS access for non-citizens can be limited.

checklist.title: Ministry of Labour (MTE/SINFRE) work authorisation obtained
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer applies via SINFRE. Allow 4–8 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: Critical path item — start immediately after offer is confirmed.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract (CLT or assignment agreement)
checklist.notes_employee: Required for MTE application and consulate visa.
checklist.notes_hr: Specify contract type — CLT (direct hire) or assignment/secondment.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 6 months beyond intended stay.

checklist.title: Consulate appointment booked for VITEM V
checklist.notes_employee: Book at the Brazilian consulate in your country of residence after MTE authorisation is granted.
checklist.notes_hr: Lead time varies by consulate — book at T-8 weeks.

checklist.title: VITEM V visa application submitted
checklist.notes_employee: Bring: passport, MTE authorisation, employment contract, biometric photos, police clearance certificate.
checklist.notes_hr: Track application; prepare for additional document requests.

checklist.title: VITEM V visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check validity dates and entry conditions. First entry must be within validity window.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy for HR file; confirm planned entry date.

checklist.title: CRNM registration at Federal Police (within 90 days of arrival)
checklist.notes_employee: Register at the nearest Federal Police (Polícia Federal) unit with passport, visa, photos, and employment contract. Do not miss the 90-day deadline.
checklist.notes_hr: Monitor 90-day clock from arrival date; delays result in fines and irregular status.

checklist.title: CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas) registered with Receita Federal
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at a Receita Federal office or Banco do Brasil branch. Required for bank account and payroll.
checklist.notes_hr: CPF is needed before payroll can run legally.

checklist.title: Private health insurance enrolled
checklist.notes_employee: Public SUS access may be limited — private plano de saúde is strongly recommended.
checklist.notes_hr: Check whether employer provides health plan; confirm coverage starts from first day.

milestones.title: Kickoff — MTE employer authorisation
milestones.body_employee: HR initiates the work authorisation request with Brazil's Ministry of Labour (SINFRE/MTE). This is the critical-path step.
milestones.body_hr: File MTE application immediately — 4–8 week process before consulate can be approached.

templates.route_title: Italy — Nulla Osta / National Visa + Permesso di Soggiorno
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals require a Nulla Osta (work authorisation) issued by the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione, followed by a National (Type D) visa at the Italian consulate. Within 8 working days of arrival, you must submit a Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit) application at the Post Office or Questura. EU/EEA nationals need only an Iscrizione anagrafica. All workers need a Codice Fiscale (tax code) and Residenza registration.
templates.hr_summary: Nulla Osta is the critical path item for non-EU/EEA employees — apply via the Sportello Unico as soon as the job offer is confirmed, as processing can take 8–16 weeks. The Permesso di Soggiorno 8-working-day window after arrival is legally strict. EU Blue Card is available for high earners (salary ≥ €32,000/year for 2024).
templates.internal_notes_hr: Italy's Decreto Flussi (annual quota decree) restricts some non-EU work visa categories — confirm the route is open. The Codice Fiscale is required for payroll, contracts, banking, and rental agreements. Permesso di Soggiorno can take 3–6 months to be issued but the kit receipt (ricevuta) is accepted as proof in the meantime.
watchouts: Nulla Osta from the Sportello Unico can take 8–16 weeks — start immediately after job offer is confirmed.
Permesso di Soggiorno application must be submitted within 8 working days of arrival — missing this window creates irregular status.
The kit receipt (ricevuta del kit postale) acts as temporary proof while the Permesso is processed (3–6 months).
Codice Fiscale is required for payroll, contracts, banking, and leases — obtain it as soon as possible.
Decreto Flussi annual quotas may restrict certain non-EU work categories — confirm route availability in advance.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract confirming role and salary
checklist.notes_employee: Required for Nulla Osta application.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm salary meets EU Blue Card threshold (€32,000+) if applicable.

checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 3 months beyond intended stay.

checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Italian consulate in your country of residence. Bring: Nulla Osta, passport, contract, photos, medical certificate.
checklist.notes_hr: Lead time varies by consulate — book immediately after Nulla Osta is granted.

checklist.title: National (Type D) visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check validity window and permitted activities.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy; align start date with visa validity.

checklist.title: Permesso di Soggiorno application submitted (within 8 working days of arrival)
checklist.notes_employee: Purchase and submit the kit at any post office (Poste Italiane) within 8 working days of arrival. Bring passport, visa, Nulla Osta, photos, and contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Monitor the 8-day window strictly; retain kit receipt (ricevuta) as interim proof.

checklist.title: Codice Fiscale (Italian tax code) obtained from Agenzia delle Entrate
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Agenzia delle Entrate or Italian consulate abroad. Required for payroll, contracts, and banking.
checklist.notes_hr: Obtain before first payroll run.

checklist.notes_employee: Register at your local Comune (municipal office) within 20 days of establishing residence.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for some banking and public services.

checklist.notes_employee: Enrol in the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) at your local ASL. Requires Codice Fiscale and Permesso di Soggiorno kit receipt.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm employer health benefit coverage from day one.

milestones.body_employee: HR initiates the Nulla Osta work authorisation request at the Sportello Unico. This is the critical path step.
milestones.body_hr: File with Sportello Unico immediately — processing takes 8–16 weeks. Confirm quota availability under Decreto Flussi.

milestones.body_employee: Attend Italian consulate with full pack: Nulla Osta, passport, contract, photos, medical certificate.
milestones.body_hr: Track application; prepare for supplemental document requests.

milestones.title: Type D visa granted
milestones.body_employee: Check visa validity. Plan entry date accordingly.
milestones.body_hr: Retain copy; update compliance record; confirm start date.

milestones.title: Arrival & Permesso di Soggiorno kit
milestones.body_employee: Arrive in Italy. Within 8 working days, buy the Permesso di Soggiorno kit at Poste Italiane and submit your application. Keep the ricevuta as proof.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm arrival; monitor 8-day window; support with Poste Italiane visit if needed.

milestones.title: Codice Fiscale, Residenza & healthcare
milestones.body_employee: Obtain Codice Fiscale from Agenzia delle Entrate. Register Residenza at local Comune. Enrol in ASL healthcare.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm Codice Fiscale is on file before payroll run; schedule 3-month check-in.

milestones.title: Permesso di Soggiorno issued & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Collect Permesso di Soggiorno card (typically 3–6 months after application). Open bank account, finalise rental contract.
milestones.body_hr: File Permesso di Soggiorno copy; update renewal calendar (typically valid 2 years, then renewable).

templates.route_title: Spain — Work & Residence Authorisation / NIE / TIE
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals require a combined work and residence authorisation (autorización de residencia y trabajo por cuenta ajena) initiated by the employer in Spain, followed by a visa at the Spanish consulate. After arrival, you obtain your NIE (foreigner ID), complete Empadronamiento (municipal registration), and apply for the TIE (residence card). EU/EEA nationals only need NIE, Empadronamiento, and EU registration certificate. All workers need a Social Security number.
templates.hr_summary: The employer must file the work and residence authorisation application in Spain as the critical path step (allow 1–3 months). Ensure NIE, Empadronamiento, and TIE steps are completed promptly after arrival. Social Security number registration must precede payroll.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Non-EU/EEA nationals: the autorización is issued in Spain by the immigration office (Delegación del Gobierno), then the employee collects their visa at the Spanish consulate abroad. NIE is the core identifier used in all Spanish official processes. TIE replaces the old green certificate for non-EU nationals. Highly Qualified Professional (EU Blue Card) route available for salaries ≥ 1.5× average salary.
watchouts: The employer-filed work and residence authorisation can take 1–3 months — start immediately after offer is confirmed.
NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) is required for almost all Spanish official and commercial transactions.
Empadronamiento (municipal registration) is required for healthcare access, school enrolment, and many administrative processes.
TIE application must be submitted within 30 days of entering Spain on the work visa.
Social Security number must be registered before payroll can run — obtain via employer or INSS office.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract
checklist.notes_employee: Required for the work and residence authorisation application.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm contract specifies role, salary, and work location in Spain.

checklist.title: Work and residence authorisation (autorización de residencia y trabajo) application filed
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer files with the Delegación del Gobierno in Spain. Allow 1–3 months.
checklist.notes_hr: Critical path — initiate immediately after offer is signed. Track expediente number.

checklist.title: Work and residence authorisation granted
checklist.notes_employee: Employer receives resolution; you can then apply for the visa at the Spanish consulate.
checklist.notes_hr: Send resolution to employee promptly; consulate step must follow within validity window.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 1 year beyond the intended stay.

checklist.title: Spanish work/residence visa obtained at consulate
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Spanish consulate in your country of residence with the authorisation resolution.
checklist.notes_hr: The visa is typically valid for 90 days entry — must be used within this window.

checklist.title: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) obtained
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the local Policía Nacional comisaría or via consulate. Required for all official and commercial transactions in Spain.
checklist.notes_hr: NIE is the key identifier — payroll, bank accounts, and lease agreements all require it.

checklist.title: Empadronamiento (municipal address registration) completed
checklist.notes_employee: Register at your local Ayuntamiento (town hall) with passport, visa, and rental contract. Required for healthcare and school enrolment.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm registration; needed for healthcare access from day one.

checklist.title: TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) residence card application submitted
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Policía Nacional within 30 days of entering Spain. Bring: passport, visa, NIE, Empadronamiento certificate, photos, and employment contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain appointment receipt as interim proof; TIE takes 4–6 weeks to issue.

checklist.title: Social Security number (Número de Afiliación) registered
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer registers you with the INSS (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social) before your first working day.
checklist.notes_hr: Required before payroll — employer registers affiliation number at INSS.

milestones.title: Kickoff — work and residence authorisation application
milestones.body_employee: HR files the work and residence authorisation with the Delegación del Gobierno in Spain. This is the critical path step.
milestones.body_hr: File autorización de residencia y trabajo immediately — processing can take 1–3 months.

milestones.title: Authorisation granted
milestones.body_employee: HR sends you the resolution. Book your consulate appointment promptly — the resolution has a validity window.
milestones.body_hr: Send resolution to employee; ensure they book consulate within validity window.

milestones.title: Consulate appointment & visa obtained
milestones.body_employee: Visit Spanish consulate with resolution, passport, photos, and supporting documents. Collect visa.
milestones.body_hr: Track visa collection; confirm planned entry date.

milestones.title: Arrival in Spain
milestones.body_employee: Enter Spain. The 30-day TIE application window starts from entry.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival date; set TIE 30-day reminder immediately.

milestones.title: NIE, Empadronamiento & Social Security
milestones.body_employee: Obtain NIE at Policía Nacional. Complete Empadronamiento at Ayuntamiento. Employer registers your Social Security affiliation (INSS).
milestones.body_hr: Confirm NIE and Social Security number on file before first payroll run.

milestones.title: TIE application submitted
milestones.body_employee: Apply for TIE (residence card) at Policía Nacional within 30 days of entry. Retain appointment receipt as interim proof.
milestones.body_hr: File appointment receipt; TIE card typically issued in 4–6 weeks.

milestones.title: TIE received & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Collect TIE card. Open Spanish bank account. Enrol children in school if applicable. Schedule 3-month check-in.
milestones.body_hr: File TIE copy; update TIE renewal calendar (typically valid 1–2 years, then renewable); confirm payroll and healthcare active.
